quality: A 62" lamp with a turned wood stem of stacked balls on a round wood base, under a cream linen drum shade. The 3-way rotary switch gives low, medium and high with a 3-way bulb. Because it's natural wood, grain and tone vary from lamp to lamp.

Adesso designs for the mass and mid market, so expect solid everyday quality rather than heirloom craft. The same design comes in a black wood finish (3932-01) and as a matching 28" table lamp (Orchard 3931-12).

maker.name: Adesso
paragraphs: Adesso, Italian for "now," was founded in New York City in 1994 by Lee Schaak, who leads its design, and Peggy Traub, a former Bloomingdale's merchandising executive. It set out to make contemporary home products at moderate prices and now sells lamps and ready-to-assemble furniture through everyone from mass merchants to upscale lighting stores.

Adesso rarely credits individual designers on its everyday lines, though its ADS360 studio collaborates with outside designers on select pieces. The Orchard collection appears in retailer listings from around spring 2023.

items.name: Vintage French bobbin floor lamps (1940s)
items.why: The stacked, lathe-turned bobbin stem comes from traditional French and Spanish woodturning. No single designer owns it; the Orchard is a modern factory version of that tradition.

similar.note: I didn't find a solid-wood bobbin floor lamp that's clearly better made at a reasonable price. RH's oak Alden has the look but is a $1,075 table lamp.
